name: Great Vow Zen Monastery
tradition: Soto Zen in the White Plum lineage of Taizan Maezumi Roshi, enriched by Tibetan and Theravada influences.
teacherAccess: Abbots Jan Chozen Bays Roshi and Hogen Bays Roshi lead alongside other ZCO teachers, with one-on-one interviews (sanzen) offered during retreats.
retreatOptions: Monthly weeklong silent sesshin (6-10 days), weekend retreats, workshops, year-round guest stays, and a full-time residential monastic program.
about: Great Vow Zen Monastery is a residential community of lay and ordained practitioners engaged in around-the-clock Buddhist practice, located 80 miles northwest of Portland on 40 forested acres overlooking the Columbia River flood plain. Its practice heritage is the White Plum Soto/Rinzai lineage of Taizan Maezumi Roshi, enriched by teachings from the Tibetan and Theravada traditions. The monastery includes a spacious meditation hall, guest and resident dormitories, a dining hall, an organic vegetable garden, and the well-known Jizo Garden memorial. Each month it holds a weeklong silent sesshin, and it also offers weekend retreats, workshops, and overnight guest stays for those wishing to sample monastic life. A public Sunday Program with chanting, meditation, and a dharma talk is open to all.
technique: Zazen (seated Zen meditation), typically 8-10 hours daily during sesshin, with walking meditation, work practice, formal oryoki meals, and teacher interviews.
schedule: Sesshin days run roughly 4:20 a.m. to 10 p.m. in silence, with sitting in two-hour blocks of four 25-minute periods, a morning work period, meals, and a dharma talk (teisho).
cost: Weeklong sesshin about $280-$380 total (sliding scale); a $50 deposit holds a space with the balance due on arrival; some sesshin are donation-only.

pricePerDay.notes: July 2026 6-night sesshin (Mon 5pm-Sun 1pm) priced $280-$380 total, divided by 6 nights.

foodNotes: Vegetarian meals that may contain eggs and dairy; vegan, gluten-free, and dairy-free options usually provided on request.
workNotes: A morning work period of roughly 90 minutes (cooking, cleaning, gardening, or sewing) is part of sesshin and residential practice.
